title: One relaunch. Many connected decisions.
voice: A product relaunch is not a single switch. Supply, assortment, customer codes, and approvals must move together, often across different teams.
caption: A relaunch connects supply, assortment, codes and approvals.
detail: The business challenge: keeping one change visible across handoffs.

title: Make the handoff visible
voice: When those handoffs are fragmented, the next team can miss what changed. The portal brings the linked work into a traceable view.
caption: Trace the change across teams instead of losing the handoff.
detail: Connected views support coordination; they do not replace human approval.

title: Start with the network lifecycle
voice: Network Planning follows a material through its lifecycle. Teams can inspect the predecessor and successor, the change type, and the intended network dates.
caption: Predecessor → successor, change type and lifecycle dates.
detail: Material-level context follows the network change.

title: See where supply is affected
voice: Sourcing and distribution views show which geographies, depots, and channels are in scope. Readiness is checked before a request moves onward.
caption: Geographies, depots and channels define the affected network.
detail: Readiness is evidence for review, not an automatic release.

title: Review before advancing
voice: A service request carries the proposed change into review. Status and approval keep the decision explicit, so teams can distinguish planned work from accepted work.
caption: A service request makes approval and status explicit.
detail: The workflow preserves the distinction between proposal and approval.

title: Translate the change to assortment
voice: Paid Bible connects basepacks and materials to the places they must be sold. Teams see the geography and channel combinations that need attention.
caption: Basepack × material × geography × channel.
detail: Assortment scope can be compared with the network plan.

title: Track readiness, not just intent
voice: Readiness and request review expose the remaining work. That helps a reviewer see what is configured, what is pending, and what still needs a decision.
caption: Configured, pending and reviewed are different states.
detail: Visible state helps avoid treating a draft as a completed listing.

title: Connect old and new customer codes
voice: CCR then focuses on customer-code continuity. Predecessor and successor CBUs, chain-specific mappings, and SAP-update status make the commercial handoff reviewable.
caption: Predecessor → successor CBU; mapping and SAP status.
detail: Status is tracked; this video does not imply automatic SAP posting.

title: First, distinguish export from refresh
voice: At MT Listing, Export ATP Payload downloads JSON built from output records. Its last-run timestamp is stored in this browser. It does not fetch live ATP.
caption: JSON export from output records ≠ live ATP refresh.
detail: Current behavior: browser-side export; no fresh SAP ATP fetch.
label: CURRENT APP BEHAVIOR

title: Inspect the batch-level example
voice: The detail view demonstrates ATP criteria by customer code, CBU, depot, and batch. It checks stock age against valid days and whether pricing is valid.
caption: Batch example: freshness + pricing determine usable ATP.
detail: Illustrative values are generated deterministically, not read from a live feed.
label: DETERMINISTIC EXAMPLE

title: Rules outrank a bigger number
voice: In the guided exception demo, customer classification and the change-type ruleset come first. Missing rules, a new CIC requirement, or rundown can stop a proposal.
caption: Classify → match rules → apply hard gates.
detail: The guided exception flow uses fixtures and does not write to CCR or SAP.
label: GUIDED DEMO · NO LIVE WRITES

title: Compare only eligible candidates
voice: The demo compares usable successor ATP with eligible alternatives at the depot. National non-listing cases also check days of holding and the CLOT gate.
caption: Eligibility and national gates can override higher example ATP.
detail: The example is rules-led, not an unrestricted highest-ATP choice.
label: GUIDED DEMO · DUMMY ATP

title: Present an outcome for review
voice: The result can retain, switch, defer, or escalate a mapping. The demo presents a before-and-after proposal for human review; it never executes the change.
caption: Retain / switch / defer / escalate → human review.
detail: No simulated decision is posted to live CCR or SAP.
label: GUIDED DEMO · REVIEW ONLY

title: Keep the foundations in view
voice: Admin Center supports the reference data and access behind these workflows. Clear ownership of those foundations helps teams interpret the same change consistently.
caption: Reference data and access support consistent decisions.
detail: Administrative foundations support the portal's operational views.

title: One connected view of the work
voice: Together, these views let teams follow a relaunch from network plan to assortment and customer-code mapping, while keeping exceptions and approvals visible.
caption: Follow the change. See the exception. Keep the decision visible.
detail: Visibility and coordination, with decisions still in human hands.

title: From change to a reviewable decision
voice: The aim is straightforward: fewer ambiguous handoffs, a clearer record of what is ready, and better context for the people making the next decision.
caption: A clearer record for the next human decision.
detail: Network Planning  /  Paid Bible  /  CCR  /  Admin Center
